title: Complex cystic renal masses: characterization with contrast-enhanced US.
reference_standard: surgery (9 patients) and imaging follow-up (31 patients, 12-24 months)
ct_detector: single-detector (Somatom Plus 4, n=9) and multi-detector row (Somatom Sensation 16, n=31)

title: Evaluation of cystic renal masses: comparison of CT and MR imaging by using the Bosniak classification system.
setting: NYU Medical Center, New York, USA (single center, with some external referrals)
cyst_selection: Patients referred for MR imaging of kidneys with 'cyst' or 'cystic neoplasm' in final assessment, cross-referenced with those who also had dedicated CT within 1 year of MRI. Excluded: 4 lesions with indeterminate CT enhancement diagnosed as simple cysts at MRI.
reference_standard: Surgical pathology (n=25: 20 malignant, 5 benign); follow-up imaging for non-surgical lesions
ct_detector: HiSpeed Advantage or CT/i (GE) or Volume Zoom (Siemens); 2.5-5.0mm section thickness
mr_field_strength: 1.5T (Siemens Vision or Symphony; 2 patients at 1.0T outside)
mr_sequences: T1W gradient-echo, T2W half-Fourier single-shot turbo spin-echo, 3D fat-suppressed T1W VIBE (pre and 3-5min post gadopentetate dimeglumine 20mL); subtraction imaging

title: MRI evaluation of complex renal cysts using the Bosniak classification: a comparison to CT.
reference_standard: histopathology (Bosniak III/IV) or follow-up >=24 months (Bosniak II/IIF)

title: Bosniak classification system: a prospective comparison of CT, contrast-enhanced US, and MR for categorizing complex renal cystic masses.
setting: Urology clinic, Fredericia Hospital, Fredericia, Denmark (single center)
cyst_selection: Consecutive patients from Urology clinic with complex renal cyst Bosniak >=II on prior triple-phase CT, normal kidney function (eGFR >60). Excluded: contrast allergy, CI to MRI/CEUS, prior renal surgery/biopsy, pregnancy/breastfeeding.
reference_standard: CT consensus by three radiologists (25, 20, 5 years experience) as gold standard; pathology available for 6 surgical lesions
mr_sequences: T2 TSE (transversal/coronal), 3D fat-suppressed T1W THRIVE (pre-contrast, corticomedullary 25s, nephrographic 55s)

title: Bosniak classification system: inter-observer and intra-observer agreement among experienced uroradiologists.
setting: Hospital Littlebelt, Fredericia Hospital, Denmark (single center)
cyst_selection: 100 consecutive cystic renal masses selected from 550 complex renal cysts identified from 8402 CT examinations; random sampling of 120 cases from each Bosniak category (BI n=30, BII n=30, BIIF n=30, BIII n=30), plus 30 consecutive BI lesions; final 100 randomly selected from 150
reference_standard: Consensus gold standard established by two experienced uroradiologists (Readers B and C)
ct_contrast_phases: unenhanced, corticomedullary (10s post-trigger), nephrographic (65s post-trigger); occasional excretory phase

title: Complex cystic renal masses: comparison of cyst complexity and Bosniak classification between 1.5 T and 3 T MRI.
setting: NYU Langone Medical Center, New York
cyst_selection: Cystic renal lesion with at least minimal complexity undergoing contrast-enhanced MRI at both 1.5T and 3.0T within 1 year; entirely simple cysts excluded
reference_standard: only 2/33 lesions had surgical/pathologic correlation; no formal comparison performed
mr_sequences: in-/opposed-phase T1w, HASTE T2w, 3D fat-suppressed T1w pre/post gadopentetate dimeglumine (Magnevist 0.1 mmol/kg at 2 cc/s); corticomedullary/nephrographic/excretory with subtraction

title: Progression, interobserver agreement, and malignancy rate in complex renal cysts ( â‰¥ Bosniak category IIF).
cyst_selection: complex cystic renal masses (>=Bosniak IIF) identified via MDT records, radiology database, hospital records; simple cysts included for interobserver analysis only

title: Prospective comparison of use of contrast-enhanced ultrasound and contrast-enhanced computed tomography in the Bosniak classification of complex renal cysts.
cyst_selection: Patients referred for complex renal cysts requiring further characterization
reference_standard: histology (n=3, all malignant), CT follow-up 6-24 months (n=22 stable), gold standard CT (n=27 deemed benign)
ct_contrast_phases: corticomedullary (70s), nephrographic (3 min); 95-100 mL Omnipaque 300 at 2.5-3.5 mL/s

title: Comparison of contrast-enhanced sonography with unenhanced sonography and contrast-enhanced CT in the diagnosis of malignancy in complex cystic renal masses.
cyst_selection: Complex cystic renal masses (2-8 cm) at contrast-enhanced CT; excluded simple cysts, suboptimal CT/CEUS quality
reference_standard: surgical pathology (Bosniak III/IV, n=28) or imaging follow-up 12-24 months (II/IIF, n=12; 4 progressed and resected)
ct_detector: single-detector (TomoScan Ave1, Philips, n=21) or MDCT 64-slice (Aquilion, Toshiba, n=19)
ct_contrast_phases: unenhanced, corticomedullary (30s), nephrographic (90-110s); 120-140 mL iomeprol at 2-3 mL/s

title: Renal Masses With Equivocal Enhancement at CT: Characterization With Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound.
setting: two centers (University of Trieste; Ospedale San Bassiano, Bassano del Grappa)
cyst_selection: renal masses with equivocal enhancement at CT (10-20 HU difference) and echogenic/mixed appearance at gray-scale sonography; simple/minimally complicated cysts excluded
reference_standard: histology (30/47, 64%: 28 surgery + 2 biopsy) or follow-up (>=3 years for IIF cysts, 5 years for 1 category III cyst; 2 patients disease progression = malignant)
bosniak_version: original (Bosniak criteria for CEUS per Quaia 2008, Ascenti 2007)

title: Renal cyst masses (Bosniak category II-III) may be over evaluated by the Bosniak criteria based on MR findings.
setting: single center, Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine
cyst_selection: Patients with both CT and MR examinations who had surgical treatment with pathological diagnosis OR minimum 3-year follow-up. Excluded: patients with only CT or only MR imaging.
reference_standard: surgical pathology (n=28) or minimum 3-year imaging follow-up (n=7, range 36-41 months, average 38.57 +/- 1.98 months)
mr_sequences: T1WI dual imaging, T2WI, dynamic contrast-enhanced T1WI

title: Incidental Renal Lesions on Lumbar Spine MRI: Who Needs Follow-Up?
setting: San Antonio Military Medical Center, San Antonio, TX
cyst_selection: Consecutive patients with renal lesion >=1 cm on lumbar spine MRI completely visualized within FOV, with follow-up/prior cross-sectional imaging available
reference_standard: Dedicated cross-sectional imaging (72 CT, 30 MRI, 38 US) + histology in 9 cases

title: Superb microvascular imaging is a rational choice for accurate Bosniak classification of renal cystic masses.
setting: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, single tertiary cancer center
cyst_selection: Patients with solitary cystic renal masses
reference_standard: surgical pathology (44 cases) and radiologic follow-up (11 cases: 6 simple cysts at 27-month mean follow-up, 5 complex >=1 year)

title: Bosniak classification version 2019 of cystic renal masses assessed with MRI.
setting: single center, Stanford University School of Medicine
cyst_selection: consecutively registered patients >=18 years with cystic renal mass on dedicated contrast-enhanced renal MRI protocol and tissue pathology available
reference_standard: histopathology (all, core biopsy n=2 or nephrectomy n=57)
mr_sequences: coronal and axial T2-weighted breath-hold, axial DWI, in-phase and opposed-phase, T1-weighted fat-saturated unenhanced and contrast-enhanced at 18s, 1min, 2min, 4min (LAVA Flex/VIBE Dixon/mDIXON), gadobutrol 0.1 mL/kg

title: The Modified Bosniak Classification for Intermediate-Risk Renal Cysts in Children.
Prevalence of malignancy and histopathological association of bosniak classification, version 2019 class III and IV cystic renal masses.
cyst_selection: Cystic renal masses with tissue pathology and preoperative renal mass protocol CT or MRI; preoperative diagnosis of Bosniak III or IV; search terms in radiology reports

title: Assessment of cystic renal masses in children: comparison of multislice computed tomography and ultrasound imaging using the Bosniak classification system.
setting: Beijing Children's Hospital, Capital Medical University
cyst_selection: Consecutive pediatric patients with cystic renal masses considered indeterminate or likely malignant; underwent surgery
ct_contrast_phases: unenhanced, corticomedullary (15-18s), parenchymal (55-70s); iodinated contrast 300 mg I/mL at 1.5-2.0 mL/kg

title: Volumetric Quantitative Contrast-enhanced Ultrasonography Evaluation of Complex Renal Cysts: An Adjunctive Metric to the Bosniak Classification System to Predict Malignancy.
Direct Comparison of Diagnostic Accuracy of Fast Kilovoltage Switching Dual-Energy Computed Tomography and Magnetic Resonance Imaging for Detection of Enhancement in Renal Masses.
cyst_selection: 24 patients with 41 renal masses (17 solid, 24 Bosniak 1/2 cysts)

title: CT-based Bosniak classification of cystic renal lesions: is version 2019 an improvement on version 2005?
setting: single institution, McGill University Health Center, Montreal, QC, tertiary care center
cyst_selection: adult patients with CRL on CE-CT; balanced inclusion across Bosniak categories (all III/IV included, I/II/IIF included consecutively in reverse chronological order); excluded: <1cm,
